expectations.text: Output flags the bipartite projection pathology (clique inflation, co-membership artifacts, inflated clustering)
expectations.evidence: Problem 1 explicitly states: 'every project of size d contributes a clique of size d to the projected graph (all d(d-1)/2 person-pairs who co-participated get an edge)' and 'Clustering coefficients are artificially inflated' and 'Community detection finds the affiliations, not the collaborations: Louvain will essentially re-discover your project groupings.'

expectations.text: Output recommends SDSM or FDSM backbone extraction specifically — NOT the disparity filter (which ignores bipartite structure and is wrong here)
expectations.evidence: The 'Fix' section explicitly names both SDSM (Neal 2014) and FDSM (Godard & Neal 2022) with descriptions, and includes a bolded warning: 'Do not use the disparity filter here. The disparity filter...operates only on the projected edge weights and ignores the bipartite structure entirely...SDSM and FDSM dominate disparity for bipartite projections.'

expectations.text: Output mentions direct bipartite community detection as an alternative (bipartite SBM, biSBM, graph-tool bipartite)
expectations.evidence: 'Alternative: Skip the projection entirely' section recommends bipartite SBM in graph-tool with exact code: 'gt.minimize_nested_blockmodel_dl(g, state_args=dict(deg_corr=True, pclabel=g.vp.kind))' and also mentions bipartite modularity (Barber 2007) via cdlib.

expectations.text: Output does NOT simply validate the Louvain-on-projection plan without warnings
expectations.evidence: The response opens with 'the plan as described — project → Louvain on raw edge weights — has a few specific problems worth fixing before you run anything' and structures the entire response around three named problem sections before any positive recommendation.

expectations.text: Output explains why edge weights from bipartite projection are not the same as relationship strength (co-membership count confounds project size and individual activity)
expectations.evidence: Problem 2 is dedicated to this: 'The edge weight (number of shared projects) is not the same as how strongly two people collaborate' with a concrete Alice/Bob/Carol example illustrating how a 5-person project vs. a 200-person all-hands initiative both produce edge weight=1, and 'The raw co-membership count conflates project size and individual activity level.'
